statement.p: Find the equation of a plane that is perpendicular to the vector -2\,\mathit{\vec i}+3\,\mathit{\vec j}+3\,\mathit{\vec k} and passing through the point (2,-4,3).

static.solution: -2\,\mathit{\vec i}+3\,\mathit{\vec j}+3\,\mathit{\vec k} and passes through the point (2,-4,3), an equation for the plane is (-2\,\mathit{\vec i}+3\,\mathit{\vec j}+3\,\mathit{\vec k})\cdot (\left(x-2\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}+\left(y-\left(-4\right)\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(z-3\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}) = 0, or -2\mathopen{}\left(x-2\right)+3\mathopen{}\left(y-\left(-4\right)\right)+3\mathopen{}\left(z-3\right) = 0.
